doc.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

chapter: Early life and becoming a musician
title: Growing up in St. Louis and dropping out of Tulane
summary: Suzuki violin, St. Louis jazz peers, his mother's records, Tulane, and leaving school after his freshman year for Delfeayo Marsalis's European tour.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you have a moment growing up that you can recall where the music really made an impression on you and led you down this path?

Well I was playing violin at a young age, like three or four, the Suzuki method of classical music and stuff. And I grew up in St. Louis, and I was lucky enough to grow up in an area, University City, well the Cleetown first and then U City, and like some of the guys a little older than me were playing jazz. Like Todd Williams played with Wynton Marsalis, and Peter Martin plays piano with Diane Reeves, and Chris Thomas, a great bass player. And Todd was in Wynton’s band, so this was probably like the late 80s. So Wynton and them would come around, like when I was in high school and I kind of got into it that way. But I mean I loved the music as a kid. My mom had records. I can remember listening to — she had an Ahmad Jamal record and some Miles Davis records and the Trumpet Kings record, the Montreux. So it was around the house. But it took me a minute to really decide to be a musician you know, because I went to Tulane and was just going to be a regular person kind of.
You were just going to be a — © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
Yeah, a civilian. Yeah. Something happened and I got sidetracked and here I am, 25 years later.
Not really. It took me a minute. I used to say like oh yeah, I was going to be a lawyer. And then after a couple of years it was like no you aren’t. You’re a musician.
And how did your mother feel about your going into it?

Well I went to Tulane and then I started playing with Delfeayo Marsalis. And it was my freshman year, and I had my finals and Delfeayo had like a tour in Europe like two months. So I had to decide like am I going to — so after [inaudible] I just went. I like dropped out of school. My mother wasn’t happy about it but she is a great woman. She said, “You shouldn’t do it but if you do I’ll support you.” And now she wants like thirty tickets every show I do.
